title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 21
paragraphs: It happened by chance that the Megarians were posted in the most assailable part of the whole position, where the cavalry could best approach. So as the cavalry made its attacks, the Megarians, being hard pressed, sent a herald to the Greek commanders, who said: “The Megarians say: ‘We, O allies, are not able by ourselves to withstand the attacks of the Persian cavalry, holding the position we took at first. Even so far, by endurance and valor alone, we have held out against them, hard pressed as we are; and now, unless you send others to take up our position in our place, know that we shall leave the position where we now are.'” The herald reported this to them, and upon hearing it Pausanias tested the Greeks, asking whether any others would volunteer to go to this place and take post there in succession to the Megarians. When the rest did not wish to go, the Athenians undertook the task — specifically those three hundred picked men whose captain was Olympidoros son of Lampon.
